thread:
PagerBot: PAGER: [sev2] gpu-cluster-eu-west queue length spiked to 82 (alert threshold 50). Autoscaler failed to add capacity. Notifying on-call: Alicia R.
Alicia R.: oncall Alicia here — seeing huge queue on the inference gateway, tails are piling up. Assigning Mike for autoscale checks. 
Mike S.: grabbing logs now. basic health looks ok but autoscaler shows repeated failures to create nodes: `QuotaExceeded: InstanceQuotaExceeded` for g4dn-family.
Jess P.: any recent config rollouts against batching or cache? I see a merged PR from this morning (deploy 05:40 UTC) that touched continuous batcher + prefix cache config. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/commit/abc123
Alicia R.: listing commit diff — pinging it.
Jess P.: diff snippet:
```
- continuous_batching.target_latency_ms: 25
+ continuous_batching.target_latency_ms: 250
- prefix_cache.enabled: true
- prefix_cache.ttl_seconds: 600
+ prefix_cache.enabled: false
```
Mike S.: whoa. turning off prefix cache would massively increase KV lookups and likely evictions, especially under burst. That + huge target_latency will batch up requests into big batches and saturate GPU queues.
Ira O.: I'm seeing `kvcache.miss_rate` jump from 3% -> 78% in the last 6m on the shard telemetry. Also `batch_size` distribution moved median 8 -> 64. Logs:
```
[2026-03-15T05:51:02Z] shard-12 kvcache miss=0.78 evictions=12415
[2026-03-15T05:52:10Z] gateway queue_len=82 inflight_batches=12 pending_tokens=1.2M
[ERROR] autoscaler: create_instance failed quota_exceeded
```
Sam K.: autoscaler is trying to spin up new gpu nodes but cloud account global GPU quota is hitting limit. That explains failed scale attempts. We have both quota and config issues.
Alicia R.: immediate mitigation options?
Mike S.: plan A: create temporary capacity by borrowing from staging region (eu-central) -> migrate some lower-priority pools; Plan B: revert the config commit to restore prefix cache and lower target_latency; Plan C: fallback route to smaller quantized model for non-enterprise customers.
Jess P.: I can rollback the config change right now (revert abc123) — that'll re-enable prefix cache and restore target_latency. Reverting will trigger a rolling config update across inference sidecars, expect ~30s per shard to warm.
Alicia R.: do it. Also open a manual capacity request with infra to raise GPU quota. Sam, can you request quota increase and also start the cross-region borrow?
Sam K.: on it — submitted support ticket with cloud: INC-50121, requesting +10 GPU quota in eu-west. Also spinning up aux-pool from eu-central: `rci create-pool --from-region eu-central --name aux-eu-west-1 --gpus 6`
Customer Ops: any customer-facing impact yet? Support shows a handful of 504s on inference endpoints since 05:48 UTC for customers on hosted tier. We should page account execs for affected enterprise customers.
SupportBot: Opening incident update in #support: "We're experiencing degraded API throughput in EU; mitigations in progress. ETA unknown."
Ira O.: after Jess rolled the revert (deploy 05:58 UTC) telemetry shows kvcache.miss_rate dropping to 6% within 90s and batch_size median back to 12. Queue length falling: 82 -> 28.
Mike S.: autoscaler still failing due to quota; but with prefix cache back it's handling more requests per token and queue is draining. We're seeing GPU utilization drop from 98% -> 65% on hot shards.
Alicia R.: live mitigation summary: rollback config (complete), aux-pool creation in flight, quota ticket created. Customer impact: intermittent 504s for ~12 minutes for some customers.
Mike S.: followups I ran: looked at autoscaler logs — there's a bug with retry backoff that made it stop attempting after 6 failed creates; raising an issue: https://git.internal/r-redwood/infra/issues/4321. I'll add a hotfix to reset retry state when capacity_create_fails > threshold.
Jess P.: note: the PR that caused this was trying to optimize latency for a low-throughput workload by increasing target_latency to favor larger batches; it unintentionally disabled prefix cache during testing. We need a guard in CI that ensures prefix_cache toggles cannot be rolled without a staged canary.
Sam K.: aux-pool is up (6 gpus) and we've routed 30% of traffic to it for now. Queue at 10 and falling. I kept the aux pool restricted to non-enterprise to avoid violating contracts.
Customer Ops: Triage note: Affected customers list attached: cust-239, cust-11, cust-872. We should send an incident email to cust-239 since they had multiple timeouts.
Alicia R.: handing off to Mike for post-incident analysis and follow-ups. Handoff timestamp 06:15 UTC. Mike, you're now primary.
Mike S.: ack. I'll run the immediate action checklist: 1) confirm reverted config stayed stable 2) ensure autoscaler retry hotfix ASAP 3) follow up with quota increase 4) run synthetic load to validate batching behavior.
SupportBot: Incident update posted to status page: "Partial service degradation in EU resolved; API latency improved. We are performing follow-ups and will provide a postmortem."
Jess P.: small note — we should add automated alert when `continuous_batching.target_latency_ms` changes >x% compared to last deployed value, and gate `prefix_cache.enabled` changes behind a canary flag. I'll open PRs.
Ira O.: telemetry panel to add: `kvcache.miss_rate`, `batch_size.p50/p95`, `autoscaler.create_failures` with alerts. Also add runbook step: if kvcache miss_rate > 30% and queue>40 -> consider immediate rollback.
Mike S.: creating post-incident ticket with action items: ACTIONS: revert gating, autoscaler retry fix, quota request follow-up, canary gating for batching/cache, customer emails. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD 2026-03-15 UTC.
Alicia R.: thanks team — great fast coordination. Leaving note: oncall clear for next rotation. :thumbsup:
PagerBot: Incident cleared: queue normalized. Generated incident id INC-20260315-07.
